pulls.title: 8396910: RISC-V: Sign-extend the BigInteger mulAdd intrinsic result
pulls.author: zifeihan
pulls.body_excerpt: The RISC-V BigInteger.implMulAdd intrinsic returns its carry zero-extended, whereas its Java int result must be sign-extended to satisfy the integer-register convention. For negative carries, this can cause incorrect results in subsequent integer comparisons. This change sign-extends the result at the common exit, preserving unsigned carry arithmetic inside the loop. A regression test in compiler/c2/riscv64/TestMulAddSignExtension.java checks zero, positive, and negative carries across tail-loop and unrolled-loop boundaries. Testing: TestMulAddSignExtension fails before the fix and passes afte

pulls.title: 8394693: ZGC: `ZMountPoint::find_preferred_mountpoint` does not respect the preferred order
pulls.author: benshuai5D
pulls.activity: 新建、2 个 Review、5 条评论
pulls.body_excerpt: Please review this ZGC fix. `ZMountPoint::find_preferred_mountpoint()` picks the first available mount point that matches any entry in the preferred list, so the mount-table order can override the preferred order. For example: ```text Preferred order: /dev/shm, /run/shm Mount-table order: /run/shm, /dev/shm The current code selects /run/shm, even though /dev/shm has higher priority. ``` **Fix:** Swap the nested loops to look for the preferred mount points in priority order. **Testing:** - Added gtests to cover the preferred mount-point order - `gc/z`: 20 passed. --------- - [x] I confirm that

pulls.title: 8395707: GIFImageReader misplaces rows in interlaced GIF frames 2-4 pixels high
pulls.author: mickleness
pulls.body_excerpt: ImageIO's GIF decoder didn't decode interlaced images correctly when the height was 2-4 pixels. For a tall gif (over 8px tall), interlacing is supposed to deliver pixels as follows: Pass 1: rows 0, 8, 16, etc Pass 2: rows 4, 12, 20, etc Pass 3: rows 2, 6, 10, etc. Pass 4: rows 1, 3, 5, etc. But for a short gif (4px or less), we were computing the wrong value for `streamY` and screwing up the order rows were delivered. With this PR: we immediately move on to the appropriate interlacing pass so `streamY` makes sense. For example, here is some sample output from the attached test before this prop

pulls.title: 8396908: RISC-V: Disable RVV for vector lengths exceeding 1024 bits
pulls.author: zifeihan
pulls.body_excerpt: Hi, this patch add a conservative upper bound of 128 bytes (1024 bits) for RVV vector lengths, as wider vectors are not reliably supported by the current backend. When the detected vector length exceeds this limit, the JVM emits a warning, disables RVV, and resets MaxVectorSize to zero. The existing minimum-length check remains unchanged. Disabling RVV rather than clamping MaxVectorSize preserves the assumption that enabled RVV uses the hardware vector length. --------- - [x] I confirm that I make this contribution in accordance with the [OpenJDK Interim AI Policy](https://openjdk.org/legal/ai

pulls.title: 8396653: [macOS] MOUSE_DRAGGED can arrive without the button modifier, so MOUSE_RELEASED goes to the wrong component and JTextField autoscroll never stops  (typing keeps overwriting the first character)
pulls.author: yogi1967
pulls.body_excerpt: **Symptom:** On macOS, after selecting text in a Swing `JTextField` with the mouse from right to left (including the first character, and releasing just past the field's left edge), typing does not work normally. Each typed character replaces the previous one, so the field only ever shows one character. Clicking in the field clears the state. **Cause:** On macOS, `nsToJavaModifiers` reads the current button state. If a `MOUSE_DRAGGED` event is converted after the button is released, it has no button modifier, so the mouse grab is dropped and `MOUSE_RELEASED` is delivered to the wrong component

pulls.title: 8394682: ZGC: `MetadataAllocationRequest` are not processed with `-ClassUnloading`
pulls.author: benshuai5D
pulls.body_excerpt: Please review this fix. When class unloading is disabled, `ZUnload::purge()` returns early, leaving queued metaspace allocation requests unprocessed. Threads waiting in `wait_for_purge()` can hang. **Fix:** Call `Metaspace::purge(false)` before returning: ```cpp if (!ClassUnloading) { Metaspace::purge(false); return; } ``` `Metaspace::purge(false)` - existing request-processing code - false: skips chunk-manager cleanup but still processes allocation requests and wakes the waiters **Testing :** - Added `TestMetaspaceWithClassUnloadingDisabled` - `gc/z`: 21 passed - `gc/metaspace` 13 passed, 7 s

pulls.title: 8392322: RISC-V: Optimize C++ atomic loads and stores on Ztso
pulls.author: zifeihan
pulls.body_excerpt: Hi, please consider. Under Ztso, RISC-V loads implicitly have acquire semantics and stores implicitly have release semantics, so the hardware fences RVWMO needs for acquire/release are redundant. The JIT already exploits this, and OrderAccess::acquire()/ release() are Ztso-aware (they degrade to a compiler_barrier()). The overhead of this optimization is similar to what was discussed in https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/pull/33018, but it's much smaller than what that PR involved, because there's no performance penalty from the ld flag + full fence here. pulls.title: 8391909: Improve ConfinedSegmentPool Performance
pulls.author: minborg
pulls.body_excerpt: This PR proposes to improve the performance of the newly integrated confined arena cache. Confined arenas now remember the platform pool array and the pool array index used for pool acquisition. Upon closing the arena, the pool can be returned (in most cases) directly to the correct index in the confined arena cache. If the opportunistic pool index is occupied, the logic falls back to the regular path, which scans the array for an empty slot. The PR additionally proposes to add a test to make sure the unusual release path works correctly. --------- - [x] I confirm that I make this contribution

pulls.title: 8389111: C2: Use BMI2 BZHI for variable int low-bit masks on x86
pulls.author: aprilivy
pulls.body_excerpt: C2 currently lowers variable `int` low-bit masks of the form: value & ((1 << bits) - 1) to a five-instruction sequence on x86. This change adds a BMI2 matcher rule that uses `BZHI`, reducing it to three instructions. The shift count is explicitly masked with `31` because Java shift distances wrap modulo 32, while `BZHI` treats counts greater than or equal to 32 differently. A scalar JMH throughput benchmark on a Ryzen 9 9950X3D improved from approximately 0.199 ns/op to 0.185 ns/op (6.9%).
